description: THE SECOND HAPPY PATH, AND THE FIRST TRANSACTION THE SYSTEM EVER WRITES - the complete bill payment again, but on the LOWER-CASE confirmation, on a DIFFERENT account, and against an EMPTY transaction master, so the identifier originated is 0000000000000001. WHEN 'y' at app/cbl/COBIL00C.cbl:175 of the ordered EVALUATE CONFIRMI at :173-191, and the WHEN DFHRESP(ENDFILE) arm of READPREV at :487-488, which is this case's primary contribution. SERVICE. It differs from case15 - the canonical happy path whose record images, pinned instant, timestamp derivation and confirmation construction it reuses verbatim - in EXACTLY THREE INPUTS: the letter case of CONFIRMI, the account chosen from the fixture, and a TRANSACT that holds no row. Everything else is held identical on purpose, so any difference the harness reports is attributable to one of those three and not to a fourth thing that was changed at the same time. DISTINGUISHING INPUT ONE - THE LOWER-CASE CONFIRMATION, AND WHY IT IS NOT REDUNDANT. :174 WHEN 'Y' and :175 WHEN 'y' are TWO STACKED WHEN CLAUSES SHARING ONE BODY at :176-177 - SET CONF-PAY-YES TO TRUE, PERFORM READ-ACCTDAT-FILE. COBOL stacks clauses by writing them consecutively with no statement between, and the body belongs to both. case15 proves the upper-case clause; this case proves the lower-case one, and both are genuinely necessary because THE PROGRAM PERFORMS NO CASE FOLDING: there is no FUNCTION UPPER-CASE, no MOVE through a translate table and no 88-level covering both spellings anywhere in its 572 lines. A translation that upper-cased the field on receipt and kept one clause would pass this case and still be a different program - it would also accept a lower-case 'n' as 'N' by the same shortcut - so the two arms are kept apart and each is driven (practice B5, gate G30). EVALUATE takes the FIRST matching WHEN and WHEN OTHER is the default: 'y' matches at :175, so WHEN 'N' at :178, WHEN 'n' at :179, WHEN SPACES at :182, WHEN LOW-VALUES at :183 and WHEN OTHER at :185 are all unreached, and reordering the arms or letting one fall through into the next would change the program. DISTINGUISHING INPUT TWO - A DIFFERENT ACCOUNT, SLICED FROM THE REAL FIXTURE RATHER THAN INVENTED. The account is 00000000039, not case15's 00000000001, and its raw twelve-byte ACCT-CURR-BAL is 00000008430{ - the LARGEST balance in the fifty-row corpus, 843.00. src/test/resources/fixtures/acctdata.txt holds 50 rows of exactly 300 bytes and is byte-identical to app/data/ASCII/acctdata.txt, which was checked rather than assumed (gate G16). That fixture is ordered by ACCT-ID ASCENDING, so this row sits at ZERO-BASED FIXTURE ROW 38 - the only fixture of the two where index and identifier happen to correspond. The input narrows the dataset to that single row with fromRow 38 and rowCount 1, so THE SEEDED DATASET HOLDS ONE ROW AND ITS INDEX IS 0: that is why every ACCTDAT expectation below addresses rowIndex 0 and not 38. Both numbers are stated because they are different numbers - the row's position in the fixture and its position in the dataset the case seeds - and confusing them is how an expectation ends up addressing a row nobody meant to pin. AND THE CROSS-REFERENCE ROW INDEX IS 8, WHICH IS THE ORDERING TRAP. src/test/resources/fixtures/cardxref.txt holds 50 rows of exactly 36 bytes, byte-identical to app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt, and it is ordered by its BASE KEY, XREF-CARD-NUM ASCENDING - verified by sorting, not assumed - so the zero-based row index for an account is NOT the account number minus one and is NOT the account's index in acctdata.txt. All fifty identifiers 00000000001 through 00000000050 are present, exactly one row each; slicing bytes 26-36 of every row locates 00000000039 at ZERO-BASED ROW 8, carrying customer 000000039 and card 2745303720002090, which is the value TRAN-CARD-NUM receives at :225. THE CONTRAST IS THE POINT: this account is row 38 of the account master and row 8 of the cross-reference, and a case that reused one index for both would seed the wrong customer's card into the transaction while every width still summed correctly. AND THE ROWS ARE SEEDED AT 36 BYTES, DELIBERATELY UNPADDED: app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy declares fifty - XREF-CARD-NUM X(16) at 1-16, XREF-CUST-ID 9(09) at 17-25, XREF-ACCT-ID 9(11) at 26-36 and FILLER X(14) at 37-50 - and the fixture omits that trailing FILLER, making it the one fixture of the nine that is not faithful to its copybook (gate G16, risk R-F). parity/FieldDiffer is the declared SOLE OWNER of the 36-to-50 right-pad, applied once at SEED time through the CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation this case declares against CXACAIX. Pre-padding the rows here would double-apply it and produce a 64-byte row. DISTINGUISHING INPUT THREE - TRANSACT HOLDS NO ROW, AND THAT IS A POSITIVE ASSERTION. The input declares empty: true with recordLength 350 and copybook CVTRA05Y rather than an empty rows list, because OMISSION AND EMPTINESS ARE DIFFERENT ASSERTIONS: an omitted dataset is one the case says nothing about, while an empty one states that the unit opened a real dataset of 350-byte records and reached end of file on its first read - which is the only way to reach the arm at :487-488, and no seeded row can produce it. THERE IS NO ASCII FIXTURE FOR THE TRANSACTION MASTER: app/data/ASCII holds exactly nine files - acctdata, carddata, cardxref, custdata, dailytran, discgrp, tcatbal, trancatg and trantype - and none of them is a transaction master, which is why case15 declares its one master row inline at the copybook width and why this case declares none at all. No tenth fixture was requested (AAP 0.4.9 fixes the count at nine). THE STARTBR ON AN EMPTY DATASET - A JUDGEMENT, RECORDED AS ONE. :212 MOVE HIGH-VALUES TO TRAN-ID fills the PIC X(16) key with sixteen bytes of the highest value the collating sequence has, which under the explicitly named US-ASCII code page of the nine fixtures is 0xFF sixteen times - the figurative constant, not the literal characters 'HIGH-VALUES'. It is recorded rather than encoded, because what CICS does with a high-values RIDFLD is 'position past the last record', and an UNANCHORED BACKWARD BROWSE expresses that in a way any code page can carry; US-ASCII has no mapping for 0xFF at all, so a literal key would be refused by the strict encoder before it reached a statement. That is why no key literal appears in the expectation. :213 then performs STARTBR-TRANSACT-FILE, whose EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD at :451-467 has three arms - NORMAL at :452, NOTFND at :454-459 with 'Transaction ID NOT found...', and WHEN OTHER at :460-466 - AND WHICH ARM AN EMPTY DATASET TAKES IS NOT A LITERAL READING OF THE COBOL, SO THE REASONING IS STATED HERE. TransactionRepository.startBrowse(BrowseDirection) POSITIONS BY VALUE AND PERFORMS NO BACKEND CALL AT ALL - it holds no cursor open, which is what keeps the online layer free of server-side conversation state (AAP rule R6) - and it therefore REPORTS NO STATUS, by design and documented on the method: all three STARTBR sites in the estate capture RESP and RESP2 and the paragraph that follows never tests them for a successful position, so surfacing a status would invite a caller to branch on something the COBOL ignores. BillPaymentService records the consequence as STARTBR_POSITIONING_OUTCOME = Outcome.OK: the successful arm is the only one a Java execution reaches from seeded data, THE GUARD CHAIN BEGINS AT THE FIRST READ, and the NOTFND and WHEN OTHER arms are KEPT rather than deleted - deleting an arm of an ordered EVALUATE would change the guard chain - and are driven directly through startbrTransactFile(state, outcome). THIS CASE THEREFORE TAKES THE NORMAL-THEN-ENDFILE PATH, and the NOTFND arm, which needs a forced outcome rather than an empty dataset, is a sibling case's subject and is deliberately not reached here (practice B12). THE ENDFILE ARM, WHICH IS EMPHATICALLY NOT AN ERROR. :214 performs READPREV-TRANSACT-FILE - EXEC CICS READPREV DATASET(WS-TRANSACT-FILE) INTO(TRAN-RECORD) LENGTH(LENGTH OF TRAN-RECORD) RIDFLD(TRAN-ID) KEYLENGTH(LENGTH OF TRAN-ID) RESP(WS-RESP-CD) RESP2(WS-REAS-CD) at :474-482 - and the EVALUATE at :484-496 takes its SECOND arm, WHEN DFHRESP(ENDFILE) at :487, whose entire body is MOVE ZEROS TO TRAN-ID at :488 (gate G47). THIS IS THE ONLY RESP ARM IN THE WHOLE PROGRAM THAT HANDLES A NON-NORMAL CONDITION WITHOUT SETTING THE ERROR FLAG, WITHOUT MOVING A MESSAGE AND WITHOUT A SEND. It raises no flag, so the :208 guard stays open and the payment proceeds; it emits no text, so nothing is added to WS-MESSAGE; it sends no screen, so the send count is unaffected. No error expectation is declared for it, because there is no error (practice B5). In Java the browse step classifies an empty result with emptyMeansEndOfFile true and returns end of file rather than not found - the single difference between a browse step and a keyed read - which is FileStatus ENDFILE, response 20, and readprevTransactFile takes its isEndOfFile branch and moves the sixteen character zeros into the record identification field. Contrast the WHEN OTHER arm at :489-495, which does DISPLAY 'RESP:' WS-RESP-CD 'REAS:' WS-REAS-CD, sets the flag, moves 'Unable to lookup Transaction...' and sends: none of that happens here. THE BARE ENDBR. :215 performs ENDBR-TRANSACT-FILE, which at :503-505 is EXEC CICS ENDBR DATASET(WS-TRANSACT-FILE) AND NOTHING ELSE - NO RESP OPTION, NO RESP2, NO EVALUATE AND NO ERROR HANDLING OF ANY KIND. That absence is preserved and not repaired: no failure arm is invented for it, no outcome is classified, and the expectation records nothing for it because the program observes nothing. Ending it makes no backend call either, because none is owed - a browse holds only a position - and ending an already-ended browse does nothing. THE IDENTIFIER ORIGINATION, WHICH IS THE VALUE THIS CASE TURNS ON. :216 MOVE TRAN-ID TO WS-TRAN-ID-NUM moves the PIC X(16) key into the PIC 9(16) counter at :57 - a cross-representation move at EQUAL width, so no digit is lost - and TRAN-ID now holds 0000000000000000, sixteen character zeros put there by :488, so the counter is ZERO. :217 ADD 1 TO WS-TRAN-ID-NUM, the program's only non-monetary arithmetic, makes it ONE. :219 MOVE WS-TRAN-ID-NUM TO TRAN-ID renders it back into the PIC X(16) field ZERO-PADDED ON THE LEFT as 0000000000000001 - fifteen zeros and a one, the first identifier the system ever issues. The increment lands entirely in the units position, with no carry into any higher digit and nowhere near the sixteen-nines boundary where a PIC 9(16) receiver with no ON SIZE ERROR clause would discard its high-order digit and wrap. THE SAME SIXTEEN CHARACTERS MUST APPEAR IN TWO PLACES - in TRAN-ID of the written record and inside the confirmation :529 strings from it - and treating the identifier as anything else, a bare 1 or a trimmed 0000000000000001 shortened at either end, breaks both at once. THE ORDER OF EVERYTHING ELSE, WHICH IS A PARITY CONCERN AND NOT A STYLE CHOICE (objective O2). :156 SET CONF-PAY-NO TO TRUE before any validation. :158-167 EVALUATE TRUE finds ACTIDINI OF COBIL0AI non-blank and takes WHEN OTHER / CONTINUE at :165-166, a genuine no-op arm. :169 IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON opens and :170-171 MOVE ACTIDINI OF COBIL0AI TO ACCT-ID / XREF-ACCT-ID is ONE MOVE WITH TWO RECEIVERS, a PIC X(11) sending item into two PIC 9(11) items, and THERE IS NO NUMERIC VALIDATION ANYWHERE IN THIS PROGRAM - none is added here (practice B5). One statement fills both keys, which is why the account read at :177 and the cross-reference read at :211 address the same identifier with no second move between them. :176-177 sets the confirmation flag and performs READ-ACCTDAT-FILE, which at :345-354 is EXEC CICS READ DATASET(WS-ACCTDAT-FILE) INTO(ACCOUNT-RECORD) LENGTH(LENGTH OF ACCOUNT-RECORD) RIDFLD(ACCT-ID) KEYLENGTH(LENGTH OF ACCT-ID) UPDATE RESP(WS-RESP-CD) RESP2(WS-REAS-CD), and the EVALUATE at :356-372 takes WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :357 / CONTINUE. In Java that is AccountRepository.readForUpdate and the record is HELD until the REWRITE at :235 replaces it (gate G47). WS-ACCTDAT-FILE is 'ACCTDAT ' at :41; the dataset is addressed by the binding key ACCTDAT that src/main/resources/application-test.yml declares, never by a literal dataset name (gate G46). THE EDITED BALANCE, AND WHY IT IS NOT ON EITHER SEND. :193 MOVE ACCT-CURR-BAL TO WS-CURR-BAL and :194 MOVE WS-CURR-BAL TO CURBALI OF COBIL0AI run inside the :169 guard and outside the EVALUATE, so they fire on this arm too and leave +0000000843.00 in CURBALI. WS-CURR-BAL is PIC +9999999999.99 at :56 - a sign position, ten integer positions, an actual decimal point character and two fraction positions, fourteen bytes and an exact fit for the symbolic map's CURBALI PIC X(14) at app/cpy-bms/COBIL00.CPY:66. THOSE FOURTEEN CHARACTERS ARE NOT WHAT THE SENDS CARRY, and that is not a contradiction: :524 blanks the field again before either send happens. The edited image is asserted where it survives, on the lookup-and-prompt sibling; here it is transient, and pinning it would assert a screen the program never transmits. STAGE THREE PASSES: :197-206 tests IF ACCT-CURR-BAL <= ZEROS AND ACTIDINI OF COBIL0AI NOT = SPACES AND LOW-VALUES - a conjunction - and 843.00 is above zero, so 'You have nothing to pay...' does not fire and no flag is raised. :208 opens the last guard and :210 IF CONF-PAY-YES is TRUE. THE CROSS-REFERENCE READ IS A FINDER, NOT A TABLE. :211 performs READ-CXACAIX-FILE, which at :410-418 is EXEC CICS READ DATASET(WS-CXACAIX-FILE) INTO(CARD-XREF-RECORD) LENGTH(LENGTH OF CARD-XREF-RECORD) RIDFLD(XREF-ACCT-ID) KEYLENGTH(LENGTH OF XREF-ACCT-ID) RESP(WS-RESP-CD) RESP2(WS-REAS-CD) - note the ABSENCE of UPDATE, because nothing rewrites this record - and the EVALUATE at :420-436 takes WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :421 / CONTINUE (gate G47). app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD defines CXACAIX with DESCRIPTION(ALTERNATE INDEX TO CCXREF VIA ACCOUNT KEY) and DSNAME(AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CARDXREF.VSAM.AIX.PATH): it is a PATH over the CCXREF base cluster and not a dataset of its own, so in Java it is ONE repository with a second finder - CardXrefRepository.readByAccountIdViaAltIndex on the eleven-byte alternate key - and never a second table (gate G45). The row it returns supplies XREF-CARD-NUM and nothing else; it is read and never written, which is why the cross-reference appears in inputs and in normalisations and in NEITHER expectedWrites NOR expectedFinalState NOR expectedDatasets. THE 350-BYTE RECORD, SUMMED FROM app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy RATHER THAN FROM PROSE (practice B11). TRAN-ID X(16) at 1-16, TRAN-TYPE-CD X(02) at 17-18, TRAN-CAT-CD 9(04) at 19-22, TRAN-SOURCE X(10) at 23-32, TRAN-DESC X(100) at 33-132, TRAN-AMT S9(09)V99 at 133-143, TRAN-MERCHANT-ID 9(09) at 144-152, TRAN-MERCHANT-NAME X(50) at 153-202, TRAN-MERCHANT-CITY X(50) at 203-252, TRAN-MERCHANT-ZIP X(10) at 253-262, TRAN-CARD-NUM X(16) at 263-278, TRAN-ORIG-TS X(26) at 279-304, TRAN-PROC-TS X(26) at 305-330 and FILLER X(20) at 331-350. That is 350, the RECLN the copybook's own header states (gate G19). :218 INITIALIZE TRAN-RECORD first - alphanumerics to spaces, numerics to zero - and then the eleven moves at :219-229 in source order, which is NOT copybook order: :225 moves TRAN-CARD-NUM before :226 moves TRAN-MERCHANT-ID, while the copybook declares the merchant identifier, name, city and zip ahead of the card number. The field map below is in COPYBOOK DECLARATION ORDER, because that is the order the record's bytes are in and the order a field-for-field diff walks. Three spans are cross-width alphanumeric moves and each pads on the RIGHT: 'POS TERM' into X(10) leaves two trailing spaces, the 21-character 'BILL PAYMENT - ONLINE' into X(100) leaves 79, 'BILL PAYMENT' into X(50) leaves 38, and 'N/A' leaves 47 in the city and 7 in the zip. TRAN-CAT-CD receives the numeric literal 2 into PIC 9(04) and is ZERO-FILLED ON THE LEFT to 0002 - the opposite direction from the alphanumerics, which is the whole reason the two are not interchangeable - and TRAN-MERCHANT-ID receives 999999999 into PIC 9(09) exactly. FILLER X(20) IS PINNED, AS TWENTY SPACES (gate G21): it is an addressable span and not a gap, and omitting it would make the image 330 bytes and shift nothing after it because there is nothing after it - which is precisely why the total width is the only thing that can catch its absence, and why the complete image is pinned alongside the fourteen named fields. THE LEFT-TRUNCATING MOVE AT :224. MOVE ACCT-CURR-BAL TO TRAN-AMT moves PIC S9(10)V99 (TEN integer digits, twelve character positions) into PIC S9(09)V99 (NINE integer digits, eleven positions). A numeric receiver is aligned on its IMPLIED DECIMAL POINT, so a numeric MOVE truncates on the LEFT and the digit that does not fit is the HIGH-ORDER one - the exact opposite of the alphanumeric moves above, which truncate on the right. FOR THIS CASE'S BALANCE OF 843.00 THE MOVE IS LOSSLESS: three integer digits are needed and nine are available, so TRAN-AMT receives 843.00 intact and the subtraction at :234 yields EXACTLY 0.00. That is stated rather than assumed, because the move is NOT always lossless - a balance at or above 1,000,000,000.00 loses its high-order digit, the amount paid is a billion short of the balance and the residual is NON-ZERO - and no fixture row can reach that, since the fifty balances run from 2.00 to 843.00. The lossy shape is a sibling's subject and is not generalised from here. THE 26-BYTE TIMESTAMP, DERIVED AND THEN PINNED. :230 performs GET-CURRENT-TIMESTAMP at :249-267: EXEC CICS ASKTIME ABSTIME(WS-ABS-TIME) at :251-253, then EXEC CICS FORMATTIME at :255-261 ABSTIME(WS-ABS-TIME) YYYYMMDD(WS-CUR-DATE-X10) DATESEP('-') TIME(WS-CUR-TIME-X08) TIMESEP(':'), then INITIALIZE WS-TIMESTAMP at :263, MOVE WS-CUR-DATE-X10 TO WS-TIMESTAMP(01:10) at :264, MOVE WS-CUR-TIME-X08 TO WS-TIMESTAMP(12:08) at :265 and MOVE ZEROS TO WS-TIMESTAMP-TM-MS6 at :266. app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy declares WS-TIMESTAMP as 9(04) + FILLER '-' + 9(02) + FILLER '-' + 9(02) + FILLER ' ' + 9(02) + FILLER ':' + 9(02) + FILLER ':' + 9(02) + FILLER '.' + 9(06), which sums to 26 with separators at bytes 5, 8, 11, 14, 17 and 20. THE DERIVATION THAT MATTERS: IBM COBOL's INITIALIZE does NOT touch FILLER items, so all six separators SURVIVE the INITIALIZE; bytes 1-10 are then overwritten with YYYY-MM-DD, bytes 12-19 with HH:MM:SS, and bytes 21-26 with 000000. BYTE 20 IS THEREFORE A PERIOD - not a space and not a digit - and the microseconds are ALWAYS 000000, because the MOVE ZEROS at :266 is unconditional and nothing in the program ever writes a sub-second value. The image is 2022-07-19 23:12:32.000000, exactly 26 characters. :231-232 MOVE WS-TIMESTAMP TO TRAN-ORIG-TS TRAN-PROC-TS is ONE MOVE WITH TWO RECEIVERS, both PIC X(26), so the two spans hold the IDENTICAL twenty-six bytes: this program has no separate processing time, and a translation that derived the second from a second clock reading would differ here. DETERMINISM. The instant is PINNED to 2022-07-19T23:12:32 - the instant the program's own version footer at :571 carries, and the SAME instant case15 and every other case in this directory pins - and it is supplied by the injected Clock that common/DateHeader reads, NEVER BY A CAPTURED NOW (practice B7). A captured timestamp would make this case pass once and fail on the next run, and it would poison two spans of the written record at once. Two-digit month, day and hour, no midnight and no daylight-saving edge, so the MM/DD/YY and HH:MM:SS renderings POPULATE-HEADER-INFO derives from the same instant at :319-338 - 07/19/22 and 23:12:32 - are unambiguous and mutually consistent with the 26-byte image above. Those six header items belong to BillPaymentController rather than to the service under test, so a SERVICE case does not claim them. US-ASCII is named explicitly rather than left to a platform default, which for a nine-fixture ASCII corpus and a twelve-dataset EBCDIC one is the difference between a comparison and a coincidence (practice B8). WRITE, THEN COMPUTE, THEN REWRITE - AND THE ORDER IS PINNED. :233 PERFORM WRITE-TRANSACT-FILE, :234 COMPUTE ACCT-CURR-BAL = ACCT-CURR-BAL - TRAN-AMT, :235 PERFORM UPDATE-ACCTDAT-FILE, in that sequence and no other. THE CONSEQUENCE IS OBSERVABLE AND IS THE MOST LIKELY MISREADING OF THIS PROGRAM: the transaction is written with TRAN-AMT equal to the PRE-PAYMENT balance of 843.00, and the balance only becomes 0.00 afterwards. A translation that reduced the balance first would write TRAN-AMT as 0.00 and would be a different program. The order is asserted structurally as well as by value - expectedWrites carries the TRANSACT record at write position 0 and the ACCTDAT record at write position 0 of its own dataset, and expectedDatasets states one row on each WRITES channel - so a reversal cannot pass. THE SINGLE COMPUTE, AND WHY IT TRUNCATES. :234 is the ONLY COMPUTE in COBIL00C's 572 lines and one of the 32 COMPUTE sites in the codebase, so it carries a targeted assertion (gate G28). It has NO ROUNDED phrase - and the keyword ROUNDED appears ZERO TIMES across all 28 programs, verified - so COBOL TRUNCATES excess fractional digits on store. In Java the subtraction is exact and the store is BigDecimal.setScale at SCALE 2 with RoundingMode.DOWN, which CobolDecimal names and nothing else does. HALF_UP, HALF_EVEN, CEILING AND FLOOR ARE ALL WRONG (gate G24, AAP rule R2). Both operands and the receiver are scale 2 - a V-scale scan of all 28 copybooks returns only V99 (gate G23) - and neither is ever a double or a float (AAP rule R4). 843.00 minus 843.00 is exactly 0.00 at scale 2, so no rounding decision is actually exercised on this path; the mode is named because it is the rule that governs the store. There is NO COMP-3 IN ANY COPYBOOK IN THIS REPOSITORY - verified zero - so no packed-decimal nibble unpacking is involved anywhere in the record layer; the WS-ABS-TIME PIC S9(15) COMP-3 at :59 is working storage and is never persisted. ZONED DECIMAL, AND WHY THE BYTES ARE PINNED RATHER THAN THE QUANTITY. A signed DISPLAY item occupies exactly p + s character positions and the sign consumes none of its own, overpunched instead into the TRAILING byte; that is the only reading under which CVACT01Y sums to 300 and CVTRA05Y to 350. TRAN-AMT is therefore the eleven bytes 0000008430{ - the digits 00000084300, whose first nine are the integer part 000000843 and whose last two are the fraction 00, with '{' being a positive sign carrying a low-order digit of zero - so the value is 843.00 and not 8430.00. ACCT-CURR-BAL in the rewritten row is the twelve bytes 00000000000{, eleven zero digits and the '{' overpunch: a POSITIVE zero, which is a different byte from the '}' of a negative zero and from the '0' of the unsigned rendering. Pinning the stored image rather than a decimal literal pins the OVERPUNCH BYTE ITSELF, and the unsigned form 000000000000 decodes to the same quantity while not being what COBOL writes into a signed DISPLAY item. THE SUCCESS ARM, IN SOURCE ORDER, AND THE SCREEN IT LEAVES BLANK. :512-520 is EXEC CICS WRITE DATASET(WS-TRANSACT-FILE) FROM(TRAN-RECORD) LENGTH(LENGTH OF TRAN-RECORD) RIDFLD(TRAN-ID) KEYLENGTH(LENGTH OF TRAN-ID) RESP(WS-RESP-CD) RESP2(WS-REAS-CD), and the EVALUATE at :522-547 takes its first arm, WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :523 - the master was empty, so there is nothing for the new key to collide with and the stacked DUPKEY and DUPREC arms at :533-534 are unreachable here (gate G47). Its body runs in this order and the order is the point. :524 PERFORM INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS runs FIRST, and at :560-566 that paragraph is MOVE -1 TO ACTIDINL at :562 followed by one MOVE SPACES with FOUR RECEIVERS - ACTIDINI, CURBALI, CONFIRMI and WS-MESSAGE - each blanked at its own declared width. SO THE SUCCESSFUL SCREEN SHOWS A BLANK ACCOUNT IDENTIFIER (eleven spaces), A BLANK BALANCE (fourteen spaces) AND A BLANK CONFIRMATION (one space), even though the record's balance was just updated: the fields the user typed are cleared for the next payment, and populating them would assert a screen the program does not send. Note what is NOT blanked - ERRMSGO, which keeps whatever the last send put there until the next send overwrites it, which is exactly what lets this arm blank WS-MESSAGE and then compose a confirmation into it. :525 MOVE SPACES TO WS-MESSAGE, and it is not redundant: STRING overlays from the receiver's first byte and does NOT blank the tail. The cursor is ACTIDINL, from that MOVE -1 at :562; -1 is CURSOR METADATA and not payload - an xxxL length item is how COBOL positions the cursor - so it is declared as cursorField and not as a screen field. THE COLOUR. :526 MOVE DFHGREEN TO ERRMSGC OF COBIL0AO is the ONLY attribute assignment anywhere in COBIL00C's 572 lines, and it overrides the COLOR=RED that app/bms/COBIL00.bms declares as ERRMSG's default - the message line turns green precisely once, on success. It is recorded as HIGHLIGHT METADATA in the attributes map and not as a payload field, because ERRMSGC is an attribute item of the COBIL0AO group and carries no text. DFHBMSCA is IBM-supplied and ABSENT from this repository (risk R-D), so the mnemonic comes from common/BmsAttributes, the single reproduction of it, rather than from a copybook; DFHAID is absent for the same reason, which is where the DFHENTER mnemonic comes from. Nothing in the program ever clears ERRMSGC - the only statement that resets the output map is the MOVE LOW-VALUES TO COBIL0AO of first entry, and this is a re-entry - so BOTH sends carry the green attribute. THIS IS THE ENTIRETY OF GATE G38's HIGHLIGHT FOR THIS PROGRAM. COBIL00C copies NEITHER CSSETATY NOR CSSTRPFY, and DFHRED appears nowhere in its 572 lines, so there is no red-and-asterisk field marking to assert and none is invented. THE CONFIRMATION TEXT, COUNTED CHARACTER BY CHARACTER. :527-531 is STRING 'Payment successful. ' DELIMITED BY SIZE ' Your Transaction ID is ' DELIMITED BY SIZE TRAN-ID DELIMITED BY SPACE '.' DELIMITED BY SIZE INTO WS-MESSAGE. Both literals are DELIMITED BY SIZE, so each contributes EVERY character it has including the TRAILING space of the first and the LEADING space of the second - which is why TWO CONSECUTIVE SPACES separate 'successful.' from 'Your'. TRAN-ID is DELIMITED BY SPACE, which takes the characters up to but not including the first space; a sixteen-digit zero-padded identifier contains no space, so ALL SIXTEEN DIGITS contribute. The result is exactly 'Payment successful.  Your Transaction ID is 0000000000000001.' - 20 + 24 + 16 + 1 = 61 characters. :293 then moves the 80-byte WS-MESSAGE over the 78-byte ERRMSGO, so the value asserted on each send is those characters left-justified and space-padded to exactly 78; the two-byte loss is the picture difference between PIC X(80) and PIC X(78) and not a shortened expectation, and with spare room nothing of the text is actually cut. TWO SENDS, ONE MESSAGE, AND BOTH CHANNELS RECORDED. :532 PERFORM SEND-BILLPAY-SCREEN is send #1, from inside the WRITE's success arm. Control then returns to :234 and :235, and :242 PERFORM SEND-BILLPAY-SCREEN fires again UNCONDITIONALLY - it sits after the END-IF at :240, so it runs on both halves of the :210 branch - which is send #2. WS-MESSAGE still holds the confirmation and ERRMSGC still holds DFHGREEN, so the two sends are identical in every field and BOTH are asserted: the send COUNT is itself behaviour, so expectedResponse carries an ORDERED LIST OF EXACTLY TWO, and a translation that suppressed the duplicate as a tidy-up would differ here (practice B5). expectedMessages carries the SAME PAIR IN THE SAME ORDER on the WS_MESSAGE_80 channel, at the full eighty characters WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80) at :39 declares. That is not a duplicate of the sends and it is not noise: the sends pin the 78-byte ERRMSGO the screen received, this channel pins the 80-byte working-storage field it was truncated FROM, and those two lost bytes are exactly why the two channels are distinct.
